captions.instagram:
What is pressure?

Why does a stiletto dent a floor an elephant wouldn’t, why is a dam thickest at the bottom, and why does dal cook faster under a whistle? Squash sand, cut a tomato, lie on nails, fill a dam, pump out Magdeburg’s hemispheres and dive the Mariana Trench.

→ Pressure is force divided by area: the same push on a smaller plate sinks far deeper.
→ A 60 kg person on a stiletto presses about 75 times harder than a standing elephant.
→ A sharp edge squeezes a gentle push onto a tiny area: millions of pascals, and the tomato splits.
→ Water pressure grows with depth, P = ρgh, so a dam must be thickest at its base.
→ Blood is a liquid column too: at your ankles, blood pressure is almost 100 mmHg higher.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/pressureclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: What is pressure? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Why does a stiletto dent a floor an elephant wouldn’t, why is a dam thickest at the bottom, and why does dal cook faster under a whistle? Squash sand, cut a tomato, lie on nails, fill a dam, pump out Magdeburg’s hemispheres and dive the Mariana Trench.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/pressureclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/pressureclear

In this video:
• Force on an area. Pressure is force divided by area, P = F ÷ A, measured in pascals: one newton on one square metre.
• Sharp and wide. A sharp knife’s edge turns 10 N into megapascals and splits a tomato; a blunt one squashes it.
• Deeper means harder. Under a liquid, P = ρ g h: every 10 m of water adds about 1 bar.
• An ocean of air. Air presses at about 101 kPa at sea level.
• Myths and extremes. Gauges show pressure above the air: a “flat” tyre still holds 1 atm.
